changes.headline: Tuesday settled two dollars lower, Asia reversed on an unconfirmed Ras Tanura claim, and December WCS widened to -$31.00 on two lots
changes.dek: Tuesday settles: Brent $113.88 (was $115.81 Monday), WTI $99.90 (was $101.76); two day pullback $2.84 and $3.37 from Friday. Asia at 0435 GMT Wed: Brent $115.47, WTI $101.33 (Reuters). ICE Oct 27: TMW Dec26 -$31.00 on 2 lots (was -$29.25 on 50 lots Monday); ARV to TMW December +$7.57 traded both legs (was +$7.25 on a soft December print). Diesel crack $92.35, a fourth print below $100.. Brent settled at $113.88, down $1.93, and WTI at $99.90, down $1.86 (settles, Oct 27), after Brent printed $116.26 early and faded on the Tehran talks. Overnight, Asia traded Brent at $115.47 and WTI at $101.33 at 0435 GMT (Reuters, Oct 28), up 1.4 percent, after the Houthis claimed a missile hit on Ras Tanura (550 kb/d). Saudi authorities did not immediately confirm, and a single unnamed source told Bloomberg a fire near the export terminal had been contained (via Reuters). The first Venezuelan cargo under the US-NABEP deal also unloaded in Texas on Tuesday, 1 Mbbl supplied at no cost, for sale to Exxon Mobil and Citgo refineries (Reuters, Oct 27); no Merey price was reported. Tuesday's ICE file widened December WCS a third day, to -$31.00 (ICE TMW settle, Oct 27), down $1.75 on only 2 lots, while January widened to -$29.30 on 235 lots. December's export spread narrowed to +$7.57 with both legs traded (ARV Dec -$23.43 on 485 lots); January is +$7.45. December WCS outright is $68.90. Synthetic settled +$5.95 on zero lots, an untraded mark; Friday's traded +$5.70 on 300 lots remains the verdict print. The diesel crack printed $92.35 on the validated history refreshed this edition, below $100 for a fourth print (3-2-1: $49.59). RBN's weekly recap has WCS delivered to the Gulf Coast at -$22.28 against CMA for the week ended Oct 23, weakest since October 2022, with Access Western Blend and Cold Lake at their widest in RBN's records back to 2018.
changes.balance_read: Flat price is trading claims in both directions while the Canadian front trades the balance: growing supply ramping into November apportionment at 19 percent lights and 7 percent heavies, with the traded export spread narrowing because Houston held up better than Hardisty. The inventory buffers keep thinning in the data (the reserve at 282.6 Mbbl, a 44 year low) while the crack softens from the demand side.

changes.headline: The EIA triangle is fully set for the first time: survey draw, flat poll, and a registered expectation of about minus two
changes.dek: New versus Tuesday's edition: the private survey for the week ending Oct 23 drew crude 2.031 Mbbl (gasoline +2.39, distillate +0.38, Cushing -0.453); the Wall Street Journal survey of nine analysts averages crude at -0.1 Mbbl (gasoline -0.7, distillate -1.1, runs unchanged) and the Reuters poll of eight analysts expects crude at +0.015 Mbbl; the digest's expectation was registered before the release at a draw of about 2 Mbbl. The weekly bank forecast for the week had still not published at this edition, a third day.. Today's EIA report (10:30 a.m. ET, week ending Oct 23) is the first of the episode with the full expectation stack captured in advance. The private survey (Oct 27) drew crude by 2.031 Mbbl with both product lines building. The Wall Street Journal survey of nine analysts averages crude at -0.1 Mbbl, and the Reuters poll of eight analysts expects crude essentially flat at +0.015 Mbbl. The registered expectation is a draw of about 2 Mbbl: the survey has had the direction right two straight weeks, last week the official report confirmed roughly sixty percent of the survey's magnitude, and runs are recovering as hurricane shut-ins return. The product lines carry weight of their own: a confirming official product build extends the diesel crack's slide from $92.35, and the report's PADD 2 utilization line is the next arbitration of the Whiting unit tail (PADD 2 was 90.2 percent for the week ending Oct 16). The reserve line updates the 282.6 Mbbl print, the lowest since October 1982.
changes.balance_read: The expectation gap is the trade: a two million barrel gap between the survey and the poll, with the official print landing on a market that just paid 1.4 percent overnight for an unconfirmed refinery claim. Whichever way the print surprises, it lands on thin buffers rather than on slack.
changes.publishers: Wall Street Journal / Dow Jones survey via Morningstar, Oct 27, 2026; private survey via Reuters market sources and OilPrice, Oct 27, 2026; Reuters poll of eight analysts, Oct 28, 2026; EIA Weekly Petroleum Status Report, released Oct 21, 2026

changes.headline: Joliet's reformer has finished restarting; DOE stays silent on every award; the benchmark trial has no second day news
changes.dek: The Joliet 50 kb/d catalytic reformer, offline since Oct 20, has finished restarting (IIR, Oct 27), closing the fall's last named PADD 2 outage item. DOE: the heating oil reserve bid deadline passed Tuesday with no award posted; both reserve exchange rounds remain unpublished seven days past the re-offer deadline; posted contracts at 133.56 Mbbl. No Baltic daily print for Tuesday and no verifiable second day trial reporting were found; Week 43 remains the latest Baltic weekly.. ExxonMobil's Joliet refinery has finished restarting its 50,000 b/d catalytic reformer, industry monitor IIR said Tuesday (Reuters, Oct 27). The unit went offline Oct 20; the operator said Monday the issue was still being addressed. The outage was an indirect crude demand drag with no crude unit impact reported, so the restart removes that drag and strengthens the differential at the margin. DOE pages checked directly are unchanged since Oct 23: the Northeast heating oil reserve exchange took bids until 11:00 a.m. CT Tuesday and no award or result has been posted, and neither the September exchange round nor the October re-offer of up to 17 Mbbl has a published award. Posted exchange contracts show no evidence of a move at 133.56 Mbbl lent to 13 companies. On freight, no Baltic daily assessment for Tuesday exists in public sources and the London trial produced no verifiable second day reporting, so the Week 43 weekly (TD3C WS 1208.13, TD22 $58.22 million) stands as the latest freight fact.
changes.balance_read: The slow variables are repairing on the demand side (Joliet back, PADD 2 recovering) and frozen on the policy side (no DOE award machinery has moved since Oct 13), while the freight benchmark's correction and its court case both wait on the next print.
changes.publishers: IIR Energy via Reuters, Oct 27, 2026; DOE pages checked directly, Oct 28, 2026; Baltic Exchange Tanker Report Week 43 (week ending Oct 23, 2026)

flags.title: Hormuz and Saudi claims: a refinery claim at Ras Tanura is unconfirmed; the verified hull ledger is unchanged
flags.detail: The Houthis claimed on Tuesday a missile hit on Ras Tanura, Saudi Arabia's biggest refinery (550 kb/d); Saudi authorities did not immediately confirm, and a single unnamed source said a fire near the export terminal was contained, with no damage extent or flow interruption reported. Asia bid prices up 1.4 percent on the claim. Against it, the cycle's confirmed ledger is unchanged: claimed Saudi damage has repeatedly failed to confirm (Argus, Oct 26: Shaybah and Yanbu undamaged; Kpler: Yanbu loading 2.21 Mb/d across Oct 1 to 25), the last verified hull is the tanker disabled in the Strait on Oct 23 and disclosed Oct 26, and JMIC (Oct 25) holds the Strait at SEVERE with about 492 vessels waiting. ING (Oct 28) prices a greater likelihood of re-escalation and dates the premium's erosion to getting past the Nov 3 elections without renewed US strikes on Iran. Trade the verified hulls, the loadings and the flow prints, not the claim count. Trigger: A Saudi or Aramco statement of facility damage, loading evidence of a Ras Tanura flow interruption, a named vessel or corroboration for the Oct 24 mine claim, or a tier 1 flow print stepping down

flags.title: Sanctions waiver: first US cargo at sea; November tranche is the supply test; refiners raising diesel output under new quotas
flags.detail: The first tanker under the waiver loaded 40,000 tonnes of diesel at Primorsk on Oct 22 and is heading for New York, arrival estimated Nov 7 (Reuters, shipping data). No signed supply contracts have been confirmed and no further loading has been reported. Reuters sources (Oct 26) and traders (Oct 28) say Russian refiners are raising diesel production in October after the government granted export quotas following the US agreement, and that Russian Baltic and Black Sea crude exports could fall next month as a result; no cargo was named. The announced programme runs 500,000 tonnes in November and 1 million tonnes thereafter. The binding constraint is Russian refining capacity: the Ryazan primary unit is halted since Oct 15 and the plant was claimed struck again overnight Oct 25 to 26 without confirmation. The import licence runs to Apr 7, 2027 and the waiver has no fixed expiry. Trigger: A first loading for the November tranche, a named US buyer or signed contract confirmation, a Ryazan restart report, or a move in Congress to block the arrangement

flags.title: November apportionment 19 percent lights; December call unregistered; December WCS at -$31.00 on two lots
flags.detail: November Mainline apportionment is Light 19 percent and Heavy 7 percent at Kerrobert (Enbridge notice, Oct 20), with Light 13 percent at Cromer and Heavy 16 percent at Superior. December's nowcast is naive persistence on those levels and no December judgment call is registered; nominations close Tuesday Nov 17 at 0700 MST. December WCS settled at -$31.00 on Oct 27, down $1.75, but on only 2 lots; the traded strip corroborates the direction (January -$29.30 on 235 lots) and the traded December export spread narrowed to +$7.57. The synthetic return verdict is scored on the tape: Dec26 synthetic crude settled at +$5.70 on 300 lots on Oct 23, below both pre registered lines (+$7.00 and +$6.50); the Oct 27 file marked it +$5.95 on zero lots, which does not change the verdict. Q3 volumes (Imperial and Cenovus Oct 30, Suncor Nov 3) are the fundamental check that can overrule the tape verdict. Trigger: A December judgment call registered, Q3 volumes contradicting the tape verdict, or a December apportionment notice

flags.title: Freight correction confirmed in Week 43; clean tankers at records; the TD3C benchmark is on trial in London
flags.detail: The Baltic Exchange Week 43 weekly (week ending Oct 23) is the latest Baltic print: TD3C WS 1208.13 with TCE $1,287,851 per day, TD22 at $58.22 million, TD9 at WS 666 with TCE under $210,400 per day, and clean routes at records (TC1 TCE $313,200, TC20 $336,400 per day). No Baltic daily assessment for Oct 27 was found in public sources and no verifiable second day reporting on the trial was found, so a third week of correction is unconfirmed until Week 44. The Mercuria v Baltic Exchange trial opened Oct 26: Mercuria's opening filing aired panellist and internal doubts about TD3C assessments in March to April; the Baltic countered that panellists confirmed they could assess. No judgment has been reported and TD3C continues to publish; the case is an overhang on TD3C linked settlements, not an invalidation of any print. Trigger: A Week 44 Baltic print extending or reversing the correction, a trial judgment, or a fresh fixture at a materially different level

forward_calendar.what: EIA weekly report; Louisiana refiner third quarter call; Fed decision
forward_calendar.detail: The EIA reports the week ending Oct 23 at 10:30 a.m. ET against a private survey draw of 2.031 Mbbl and a poll at essentially flat; the digest's expectation was registered before the release at a draw of about 2 Mbbl. The refiner that received the Oct 23 emergency reserve exchange reports the same day, call at 12:00 p.m. ET: the first on the record venue where the exchange's undisclosed cause can be asked. The Federal Reserve also decides on rates Wednesday.

forward_calendar.what: Imperial Oil and Cenovus Q3 results; positioning release
forward_calendar.detail: The first of the Canadian majors to report the quarter that contains the fall turnaround windows. Upstream volumes are the first public test of whether Syncrude, Horizon and the Suncor plants returned on their guided schedules; no completion notices have been published for any of them. The synthetic return verdict, scored on the tape at +$5.70, is graded against these volumes. The commitments of traders release the same day carries positioning as of Oct 27, the first vintage covering the episode's largest sessions.

forward_calendar.what: OPEC+ meeting (Nov 1 to 2, most likely Nov 2)
forward_calendar.detail: The seven core members set December levels and are expected to keep targets steady (Reuters, Oct 28, three people with knowledge of the matter). Their last decision (Oct 4) held November targets at September levels; actual output runs well below quota with Gulf exports war constrained, so the arithmetic is not the binding constraint on barrels.

forward_calendar.what: Suncor Q3 results; US midterm elections
forward_calendar.detail: Suncor operates Syncrude and the Base Plant and Edmonton refinery windows that ended in mid-October; its Q3 volumes are the closest public read on those returns ahead of September AER data. The midterms the same day are the date after which US strike expectations on Iran have been priced, and the date the ING premium condition turns on.
Vermilion reports the September quarter; volumes and any guidance change are the read.
MEG reports the September quarter; Christina Lake volumes are the read on the SAGD fleet's autumn.
Enbridge reports into the November apportionment month (Light 19 percent, Heavy 7 percent at Kerrobert); Mainline volumes and any December colour are the read.
Deliveries under the Northeast heating oil reserve exchange (bids closed Oct 27, no award posted at this edition) complete by Nov 13, refilling the reserve ahead of the 2027 to 2028 heating season.

Nominations for December close at 0700 MST. December's nowcast is persistence at Light 19 percent and Heavy 7 percent; a judgment call registered before this date is the prediction programme's second decision performance entry.
